answer: Sybil resistance rests on a scarce, non-transferable bond per identity, slashed when an independence proof fails. A worker stakes before vouching, and the amount rises with the identities it already sponsors, so the thousandth clone costs far more than the first. Work is drawn at random across staked keys, and rewards sit behind a horizon of epochs, time for auditors to correlate duplicates. Clones sharing one wallet look like a single marble among unique balls: the audit links their behaviour and seizes the whole trellis of bonds. Ten thousand fakes demand capital one sweep can erase.
